facts.fact: Kiamling 在“仓促中止的 Canton 事件”后已回香港一周，坏运气仍未断；叙述者点明她最近几天是“彻头彻尾的灾难”。
facts.anchor: Kiamling had been back in Hong Kong for a week after the abruptly curtailed Canton incident, but her run of bad luck still had not broken.

facts.fact: 约看渔船是 Archie 提出的：他要跟渔民练粤语，Kiamling 当初没当回事，只当又一趟差事（她本就作息紊乱）。
facts.anchor: When they had made the appointment, Kiamling had thought nothing of it. Her sleep patterns were erratic at the best of times, and Archie’s request to practise with the fishermen was just another job.

facts.fact: 华区又有数人遇袭，具体是裁缝学徒、一对幽会的情侣、太平山街一名妓女；三人都记不起经过，记忆模糊。
facts.anchor: A tailor’s apprentice, a pair of lovers out on a tryst, and one of the courtesans from Tai Ping Shan Street. None of them had any recollection of what had happened, their memories fuzzy.

facts.fact: 受害人的炁像焦油一样凝堵；Kiamling 逐一替他们打通经络，嘱咐喝补气汤、卧床休息。
facts.anchor: Each of them had their qi gummed up like tar. Kiamling unblocked their meridian lines, advised on revitalising soups and bed rest.

facts.fact: 妓院老板娘 Madam Yau 开始发声，要求给平民更多保护、公开呼吁立法局撑腰；但 Barrister Ng 不在，本地华人便无人代言。
facts.anchor: Madam Yau, the brothel owner, had started making noises, demanding more protection for the common people, calling loudly for the Legislative Council to back them, but without Barrister Ng’s presence, there was no voice for the local Chinese population.

facts.fact: Kiamling 亲自巡街数夜，一人顾不过来，总赶在街区另一头；她劝人入夜留在家中，拟议的宵禁却遭客栈、烟馆、妓院的东主与客人蔑视，她并未取得社区信任。
facts.anchor: For a few nights, Kiamling patrolled the streets herself, but there was only so much ground one person could cover. She was always at the wrong end of the district.

facts.fact: 有人把一桶内脏倒进水里、险些泼到 Archie；一名女子用粤语叫“叫你那个 gweilo 走路看着点”，毫不在意他正掏手帕，鱼腥味刺鼻。
facts.anchor: “Tell your gweilo to watch where he’s walking,” the woman said in Cantonese, unperturbed as Archie reached for his handkerchief. The fish smell was pungent.

facts.fact: Kiamling 先答“他不是我的 gweilo”，Archie 随即用尚可的粤语插话“我是我自己的主人”，渔妇这才发现他听得懂，他笑着致意；多数渔民背过身假装刮贝壳，等两人走远才盯着看。
facts.anchor: “I am my own man,” Archie interjected in passable Cantonese, beaming as the fisherwoman realised he had understood her.

facts.fact: 是 Kiamling 支使 Archie 去“给我们叫份早餐”，辩称他练粤语、她得早餐“双赢”；他驳不倒这套逻辑，整整肩走向食摊。
facts.anchor: “Sorry, what was your point again? You get to practise your Cantonese, I get breakfast. We both win.”

facts.fact: 饭后阿奇俯身从她头上摘东西，她盯着他看：她并不介意他靠近，只是一瞬间以为他要凑过来做别的，胃里奇怪地一翻，又提醒自己别多想。
facts.anchor: Archie leant forward, plucking something from her head. She stared at him. It was not that she minded him in her personal space, more that for a moment she thought he might be leaning in for something else.

facts.fact: 阿奇从她发间拈出东西，说“你头发里同时有蛋壳和树叶，就算按你的标准也算稀奇”；她一把夺回捏碎（原文下一段称那是一片“蛇壳”）。
facts.anchor: “It is unusual, even for you, to have both eggshells and leaves in your hair.”

facts.fact: 她自陈是驱邪者、镇鬼猎妖人，家谱可上溯数百年到“鬼王”Chung Kwai 一族；她为这血统自豪，却厌倦同一套方法与训练，想试新法。
facts.anchor: “I’m an exorcist, a ghost-quelling monster hunter. You can trace our family tree back centuries, all the way to the family of Chung Kwai, King of Ghosts.”

facts.fact: 前一夜她砍掉侵入酒馆的树、拾尽能找到的种子与坚果，盼重种能安抚被她为求效率匆匆驱走的树灵；结果她只说“这次不行”。
facts.anchor: She had spent the evening cutting down the trees that had invaded the tavern and gathering up every seed and nut she could find.

facts.fact: 阿奇不认为她固执，反称她“勇敢”、是“先驱”；她由此自认确有勇气——Au 家世代护岛，做对了没人夸，出错才被抱怨。
facts.anchor: “I wouldn’t call that stubborn. I’d call it courageous. If anything, you are a pioneer.” Archie rubbed at his chin, watching the fisherman folding up their nets.

facts.fact: 他说明来东方的缘由：这里有机会“治理而非掠夺”；他考上 cadetship、受两年密集粤语训练，如今是维多利亚女王的公务员，也自称“先驱”。
facts.anchor: “Yes. We have a chance here to do something different. To govern, not simply to strip these lands of their worth. I got a place on the cadetship, intense Cantonese training for two years, and now here I am.

facts.fact: 他把鱼肉撕碎撒给凑近的流浪狗、笑着摸狗头说“好了好了，我忠实的朋友们，想吃多少吃多少”；Kiamling 警告喂了就再也赶不走。
facts.anchor: He laughed as he petted their heads. “There, there, my devoted friends, eat as much as you would like.”
